PMID 25429463, PMC full text read. 58 primary / 108 secondary, tumors in all groups incl. mock, authors' 'questioning the usefulness' caveat all verbatim. Allele = homozygous β-major deletion (th1/th1 consistent); conditioning 11 Gy TBI, busulfan never mentioned. Corrections: model_filed should be null (P/T memo not public, only clinical memo posted); epub_year 2014 unverifiable.

But the brief scores silence: 3 MDS/AML in 54, holds 2021-02-16→05-25 and Dec 2021→2022-12-16, boxed warning, all confirmed. ad-amyloid precedent → contra; date to Goyal 2022. Keep 2020 same only as an intermediate, confidence low.

Supporting: Kanter 2023 AJH (PMID 36161320, epub 2022-10-10, print 2023) 'acute myeloid leukemia was observed in two patients in Group A and deemed unlikely related to insertional oncogenesis'; Lyfgenia label 5.1 attributes risk to 'hematopoietic stress associated with mobilization, conditioning, and infusion' plus SCD baseline; label 13.1 'No carcinogenicity studies have been performed with LYFGENIA.'

safety entry 1 note should say the model was uninformative by design, not merely untested: T-cell lymphomas in mock and vector secondary recipients alike meant it had no power to detect a vector-driven increment (authors' own caveat), it used TBI not busulfan, β-thal not sickle mice, and a 6-month horizon; the only readout it could make (oligo/polyclonal IS profile, no clonal dominance) is the one that matched in patients (VAMP4 clone 1-7%). For the harm that occurred there was no model at all.
Kanter 2023 AJH judgement citation verified: doi 10.1002/ajh.26741 = PMID 36161320; Group A '(≥0.08 c/dg) and HbA T87Q levels (≥0.46 g/dL) were inadequate for substantial clinical effect' verbatim.
rule_questions: Juxtaposed matches: every `same` in this draft has comparison_stated=false (drafter put Pawliuk beside Ribeil/Kanter). The checker brief lists 'same with no published model-vs-patient comparison' as a failure, but the house example cf-cftr scores Ramsey 2011 (patient-only trial) as `same` the same way. I followed the house example and did not downgrade engagement/efficacy; if the strict reading governs, both `same` cells become untested.

Structural silence (safety): the brief's '(or its silence)' clause plus the ad-amyloid precedent (4-species tox 'missed' BACE cognitive harm → contra) says a safety model that was silent on a harm that materialised reads contra. Here the model was not merely silent but structurally incapable: wrong disease (β-thal), wrong conditioning (11 Gy TBI, no busulfan), 6-month horizon, and a baseline lymphoma rate that masked any increment. Options: (a) contra, dated to first published malignancy (Hsieh 2020, single MDS attributed to busulfan) or to first published attribution of malignancy to transplant/disease risk in this class (Goyal 2022, my proposal); (b) 'no model for this harm' → cell stays untested with a note. The brief does not decide between (a) and (b); I applied (a) because that is what ad-amyloid did.

Dose when the model states no target: does an observed mouse level (~50%) that patients turned out to need (~40-46%) count as a matched exposure target? I read the cf-cftr dose cell ('predicts who responds, not how much' → untested) as precedent for untested; the brief's wording 'the model's exposure/occupancy target' presumes a stated target.

model_filed when the only FDA document that would name the nonclinical study (the Pharmacology/Toxicology memo) is not posted: the clinical review defers to it and the Lyfgenia page lists only approval letter, SBRA, approval-history PDF and clinical memo. Null seems right; the draft's false reads 'no carcinogenicity studies' as 'Negre not filed', which does not follow.
